methods.label: Factor before subtracting
methods.explanation:
The original denominators must be nonzero, so \(a\ne0\), \(b\ne0\), and \(a\ne b\). Factor the second fraction to reveal a common factor:
\[
\frac{ab-b^2}{ab-a^2}
=\frac{b(a-b)}{-a(a-b)}
=-\frac ba.
\]
Cancelling \(a-b\) is valid because \(a\ne b\). Subtracting this negative fraction now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{a^2-b^2}{ab}-\left(-\frac ba\right)
&=\frac{a^2-b^2}{ab}+\frac{b^2}{ab}\\
&=\frac{a^2}{ab}\\
&=\frac ab.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the reduced expression is \(\boxed{a/b}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\), with the original restrictions retained.
